Blockhold · Gameplay & map review · Ruleset 6

Clearer maps. More ways to hold the line.

Make the choice of position and counter matter. Remove difficulty caused by hidden stacking, lost support bonuses, and layouts that all ask the same question.

14 → 6Total routes across the last three maps
27 → 9Large landmarks, with fewer roadside decorations
Recorded combat comparisons in this report

What the analysis found

Healers created hidden difficulty spikes

Every Acolyte could add another 6 HP/s to a nearby enemy. The new rule takes the strongest healing aura, including staggered pulses. A dense healer column still needs a counter, but cannot multiply its sustain without limit.

Some support value was missing

Beacon damage and speed did not reach Barracks soldiers. They now apply to existing and upgraded squads, and disappear when support is sold. Overlapping Beacons choose one aura using damage and speed together.

A small leak hurt the economy twice

Losing a foe meant losing its bounty and the entire clear payment. Every resolved wave now pays its base reward; flawless waves still earn the streak bonus. Recovery remains possible after a mistake.

Keep difficulty meaningful.

The campaign HP ramp and the recent post-clear rates remain: Casual 2%, Normal 4%, Veteran 7.5% per wave. This pass addresses interactions, map readability and pacing. It does not make every tower combination equally good.

Three maps, three different decisions

Sunderfall Terraces

4 routes → 1 switchback30 × 18 board

Use the mesa to attack repeated passes. Low positions need clear angles around the cliff; the turns reward splash, blocking, and well-placed support.

Enemy counts, rewards, boss order and campaign wave counts are retained. Groups that now share an entrance arrive in distinct columns, with a minimum 0.4-second spacing.

Emberwind Reach

5 routes → 2 flanks30 × 18 board

Defend opposite sides of the lava basin, then finish survivors at the eastern merge. Keep the champion-steered firestorm away from your best towers.

Enemy counts, rewards, boss order and campaign wave counts are retained. Groups that now share an entrance arrive in distinct columns, with a minimum 0.4-second spacing.

Tidereach Causeway

5 routes → 3 crossings32 × 18 board

The central crossing stays open while the outer causeways alternate. Invest in shared lookouts or specialise on an exposed approach. Gate previews use the actual open routes, and flood overlays leave shared roads visible.

Enemy counts, rewards, boss order and campaign wave counts are retained. Groups that now share an entrance arrive in distinct columns, with a minimum 0.4-second spacing.

Compare actual combat outcomes

These are repeatable bot runs, not estimates of player win rates. A result marked “clear” used legal purchases and real combat. A loss identifies a build to investigate; it does not prove the map is impossible.

Build profileBefore · seed 71Revised · seed 71Revised · seed 193

Each profile permits different families and chooses one branch direction. The planner reacts to upcoming armor, resistance and air, so its exact mix varies by map. Normal is checked without requiring a Seraph.

Additional hero check: Liora on the last two maps

Twenty additional runs used the same legal progression budget with Liora. Her Normal clears include Combined arms and Beacon support on both maps, plus the Seraph profile on Emberwind. None of these five profiles cleared Veteran. Changing hero alone did not resolve the late Veteran concern.

Static pressure is an approximate regression alarm based on gold, lane reach and enemy HP. It omits important mechanics; it must not override real combat evidence. Short troughs give room to recover and make purchases.

Where each tower should shine

FamilyGood decisionTradeoff to preserve
ArrowAffordable air coverage; long-range precision or a poisonous volley.Heavy armor needs help from magic, poison or armor shred.
MageArmor counters; single-target stripping or chains through clustered foes.Warded enemies reward a physical partner.
CannonDense ground groups, especially held at a turn by soldiers.Needs air coverage and loses value against isolated enemies.
BarracksKeep enemies inside firing zones; a Beacon can now improve the soldiers.Blocking does not solve air. Rally placement matters more than nominal DPS.
BallistaShoot down a straight road, with an air or armor branch.Piercing value falls when targets spread across awkward angles.
BeaconSupport an expensive cluster; raise its foundation to reach another group.Buy attackers first. A basic Beacon's 10% damage bonus needs roughly 1,500 gold of comparable attackers in its light to repay its 150-gold cost through damage alone.
SeraphExpensive, compact power against crowds; physical and magic branches.Its basic ray deals about 56 DPS to one enemy versus 169 across three, before defenses and modifiers. Do not price it as if every ray always has three targets.
Method, limitations and follow-up
  • Uses the production Game.simStep at 60 Hz, actual paths, line of sight, projectiles, soldier combat, enemy abilities, tides, bounties and upgrade prices. Particle effects, sound and camera flourishes are disabled.
  • Aldric, Meteor Storm, reinforcements and his signature are available in the active pass. The Armory budget is at most three stars per previously completed map; the test does not grant a finished Armory on the first map.
  • No early calls, tower selling, manual Ballista firing lines, traps, overcharge, ascensions, hero movement or hero rank purchases. Those are additional player tools, and also gaps in this audit.
  • Seeds change combat rolls and slightly vary foundation choices. Two seeds and a greedy planner do not exhaust the strategy space. Late Veteran losses need directed playtesting before claiming every map is proven achievable.
  • Keep watching the jump into Shattered Crown, Veilscar's early air pressure, and the late tidal waves. Extend the same harness with additional heroes, deliberate rally placements and player replays rather than tuning all HP to one bot.

Design references

My design takeaway is to give each map a clear spatial premise and each tower a useful role. Ninja Kiwi's official BTD6 v51 notes distinguish cleanup, support and single-target roles, and introduce an economy-themed map. Kingdom Rush Frontiers emphasises specialised tower upgrades and different environments. These inform the direction here; the balance numbers come from Blockhold's own code and runs.

Uses Blockhold's parchment, wood and gold palette from src/style.css so the review belongs with the game. Screenshots are actual local renders. Evidence and the repeatable harness are saved alongside this review; no account save was edited on the server.
